To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the impact of information systems is heavily dependent on their use, that the use is heavily dependent on organizational culture and that the impact is heavily dependent on a match between the two.
the impact of the computer as a control system is heavily dependent on its actual use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of computer technology on organizational control systems.
the impact of information technology on the organization.
the impact of information systems on organizations, but also with the impact that organizations have on the use of information systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the computer is not an ink blot.
computerized production control is not a panacea.
the impact of information technology on organizations is heavily dependent on how the technology is used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the computer is a powerful tool for the organization, but the organization is a powerful tool to use the computer.
the computerized production control system is a kind of an ink blot.
the introduction of computerized production systems does not automatically lead to a shift from a self-contained to a vertical control style.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of information technology in organizations should be seen in the broader organizational context.
the impact of vertical information systems on the organization can be understood as an inkblot.
organizations are in a process of constant change and that this is a process that is not necessarily linear or predictable.
